Bay City, Ore April 9th 20 Mr. C. P. Pad Cushman Grades School Tacoma Wash. Dear Sir, I rec'd a letter from my son Alex Beaurais to daddy stating he got in some trouble. His letter comes from Oakville Wash. headed Chehalis day School. What is he doing down there. I want to know right away the nature of what trouble he got into and where. And I want him sent home as soon as possible if I have to pay his fare I will send you necessary money to do so. Please write to me right away and state what can be done. For I am very much worried about it. Thanking you in advance for an answer. Very truly, Remi Beaurais Rumi Beaumagis Bay City Ore. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., March 30, 1920 Mr. John H. Lehr Oakville, Washington Dear Sir: The Court has passed sentence on Alec Beauvais to the reform school at Chehalis, but has suspended the sentence on the condition that you carry out the provisions stipulated in your letter to Mr. Healey, Probation Officer. The Court understands that you are to take bodily possession of the boy and exercise the necessary supervision over him. At the request of Judge Clifford, I am asking you to come to Cushman next Saturday for Alec and take him with you, as he is committed to your care at the Chehalis Day School. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. OHK:MG Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., April 12, 1920 Remi Beauvais Box 55, Bay City, Oregon Dear Sir: I am in receipt of your letter and telegram in which you make inquiry regarding your son, Alec. In reply thereto you are advised that Alec, with two other boys, broke into a store in the vicinity of the Cushman School and stole a number of articles. They were apprehended by the police and were given a fair trial and as a result two of the boys were sentenced to the reform school at Monroe, Washington. Alec received a sentence to the reform school at Chehalis. Mr. Lehr, teacher at the Chehalis Day School, near Oakville, became much interested in Alec last summer and had Alec with him for a month. He understands Alec thoroughly and has had a knowledge of the several thefts of which Alec has been accused of. Alec made a clean breast of his failings to Mr. Lehr last summer. At that time Mr. Lehr gave Alec some wholesome advice to avoid getting into trouble in the future, but it appears that Alec did not heed the advice. I will just add that Alec was not lead by the other boys to commit this last act. In fact he admits that he was one of the prime leaders in the affair. Mr. Lehr took the matter up with the Juvenile Court in Tacoma and asked that the Court suspend the sentence on Alec and that he, Mr. Lehr, would act as sponsor for Alec if he would be turned over to him. After due consideration, the Juvenile Court suspended Alec's sentence and ordered him to be placed under the personal supervision of Mr. Lehr. Mr. Lehr is very conscientious and is thoroughly earnest in his desire to give Alec a chance to make good. He has Alec with him now and is doing the right thing by him. To Remi Heauvais, #2. I suggest that you write encouraging letters to Alec and at the same time advise him to follow the instructions of Mr. Lehr. Any averse criticism you might make to Alec in your letters will not be beneficial to him. Alec fully realizes that if he fails to make good to Mr. Lehr, that he will be turned over to the Court for commitment to the Chehalis Industrial School. The sentence imposed by the Court is from one to fifteen years, which has been suspended on the conditions above named. Alec is a bright boy and Mr. Lehr believes that by following out a course of discipline with him, and careful supervision of him, that he can make a good man out of him. From what he can learn from Alec, of his early training, he has not known the care of a mother and but little personal oversight by his father. The influence of a parent over a child either for good or bad is one of the most potent in making either good or bad men. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. Kindly deliver the paper to him. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. :MG Enc. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Cushman Agency, Tacoma, Wash. Spcl. Agt. C. U. Peel, Coakville, Wash., March 20, 1920. Dear Sir: - I have just learned that Alexander Beausais was mixed up with some other Cushman boys who entered a store in Tacoma and that there is a possibility of their being sent to a reform school. Alec was with me here several weeks last summer and I know him quite well - well enough to know that he is far from what might be termed a bad boy. This is his only offense of this nature. I am very willing to make a settlement for Alec and to assume responsibility for his future conduct if need be. In fact, I am willing to do anything to keep him out of a reform school which would be his complete ruination. I believe, on first offense, an arrangement can be made. Believing that you are as anxious as I am to keep the boy out of a reformatory, I know you will urge the matter to the utmost. If the possibility of their being sent away is as great as I am given to understand it is, I am willing to be involved in any arrangement whatsoever that concerns Alec. Very respectfully, John W. Lehr Portland Ore June 13-1919 FOR FILE Mr E Hammond Supt. Dear Sir, I am writing you in regards to Alex taking that trip. We think it will be very nice for him and you have our consent to take him. Your Friend, Mrs Emma Beausais Sept Cushman Agency Dear Sir, Enclosed please find request for the leave of my son to come home during vac. Please write and let me know what money will be needed and I will wire same to you. I notice you have my name wrong, proper is Rene Beaumais 274 WMS Ave Portland Ore. Will Alex pass for half fare on train? Dear Mr. Beausvais: The money you need to send is Alexandria's fare home. Since you paid his transportation to school, you do not have to make any deposit. Alex will require full fare. Very respectfully, 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Oakville, Wash., Dec. 17, 1919. Sept. E. H. Hammond, Cushman Agency, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Mr. Hammond: This be to ask permission for Alexander Beawais to visit me during Christmas vacation. Would it be satisfactory for him to return the Sunday following New Years? If not please state at what time. Wishing you a merry Christmas and a happy and prosperous New Year, Very respectfully, John V. Lehi. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Seattle, Wash., Dec. 17, 1919. Supt. E. N. Hammond, Cushman Agency, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Mr. Hammond: Please inform me on what date school should re-open after the Christmas vacation. Very respectfully, John W. Leht. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington, Dec. 22, 1919 Mr. John H. Lehr Oakville, Washington Dear Mr. Lehr: Alec may visit you during the Christmas vacation, leaving here December 26th. He should return in time to begin school with his class January 2nd. Your school should likewise begin January 2nd. There will be no objection to your spending money for the school children's Christmas tree, not to exceed 25¢ a pupil, if the total does not exceed $5.00; but do not spend more than $5.00. With best wishes for a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year, I am Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington June 15, 1918. Mr. Remi Beauvais 247 Wms. Ave., Portland, Oregon. Dear Mr. Beauvais, The money you need to send is Alexander's fare home. Since you paid his transportation to school, you do not have to make a deposit. Alexander will require full fare. Very respectfully, Superintendent VACATION REQUEST FOR PUPIL. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted Alexandre Beaulvais from June 15, 1918 to Sept. 5th 1918 to enable him to visit his home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Custer school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. Renni Beaulvais Father. Emma Beaulvais Mother. Guardian. Date: 6-4-18 NOTE TO DISBURSING OFFICERS.—All receipts under this agreement must be accounted for officially as Individual Indian Money. However, any forfeitures must be transferred to Miscellaneous Receipts, Class I, and deposited in the Treasury to the credit of the United States. Portland Oregon 1:58 P.M. June 16, 1918 E. H. Hammond, Superintendent. Have Alex ready for 11:35 A.M. train Tuesday June 18, 1918. I will meet him at depot in Portland. His fare is wired by N.P. railway. (signed) Remi Beauvais. If he is eligible for admission in an Indian School, I will help you in making out the application form. Tacoma Wash Dear Sir, I find it impossible for me to fill out application for the enrollment of my son, the vouchers I can not fill are no 1. as I am a perfect stranger here. I wish to ask if it would be a good plan for me to go with my boy right to you, personally, and arrange for his enrollment, as I would not like to make any mistake in filling this application for there are parts I do not quite understand, for my own education is very poor, and I am interested very much in trying to get my son in a school where he would be steady. Thanking you in advance for a reply. Yours truly, Remie Beaumais Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington, Dec. 10, 1917. Mr. Renni Beauvais, c/o Byron Hotel, 2017 1/2 1st Ave., Seattle, Washington. Dec. 4th - 1917 To Cushman Indian School Superintendent Dear Sir, On about the 10th of Sept. Mr. Brown the Sub. Agent of Indian Affairs for the Ronan District of the Flathead Indian Reservation made application to have my son in school at Cushman, which was accepted. I am now living in Seattle and working for the Gov. in the P.S. Navy yard, and I wish to know if you will except him, if I take him over or send him with someone, and will you except him on Sunday, for that is the only day I can leave my work. Mr. Brown was to inform me of the date to send him but somehow his letter to me was lost or mislaid, and did not hear from him till my wife left Polson to join me here. And he told her we could take him to school from here if we wished. So will you be kind enough to inform me if we can do so. I am Yours truly, Remi Beauvais P.S. APPLICATION OF Renee Beausais FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Alexander Beausais IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Cushman POST-OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Seattle, Wash. Date of enrollment, Jan. 3, 1918 Term of enrollment, (3) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Position, APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Tonopah, Nev., of Alexius Beaurais, M., 12, I, Remi Beaurais, of Seattle, Wash., P.O. of Los Angeles, do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to his enrollment in said school for a period of three years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Polson, Montana on May 5, 1905, that the father, Remi Beaurais, is a Blackfoot Indian of the Flathead Tribe located at St. Ignatius Agency; that he left the tribe about Oct. 1917; that the mother, Eliza Beaurais, is a Blackfoot Indian of the Blackfoot Tribe located at Blackfoot Agency, and left the tribe about 1909; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:

The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." (Act of August 1, 1914.) EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse to or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year."
